input.content: Anti-pattern: dropping a backward-compatible read branch during an in-progress, gateless schema migration. A reader that handled both legacy (top-level `address`) and current (nested `destination.address`) shapes was "cleaned up" to only read the nested shape. But the migration is incremental/bounded with no startup gate, and a supported mixed data snapshot still contains legacy rows, so the reader crashes with KeyError on unmigrated records — taking down the whole batch read (list comprehension). Signal to check: when a diff removes a compatibility/fallback branch, verify the legacy shape is actually extinct (migration complete, 0 legacy rows, telemetry) before deleting the branch; a README/contract stating "read both shapes until migration finishes" is a hard acceptance requirement. Green tests that only exercise the new shape mask this (test-coverage gap for the legacy path).
